messages:
arian: quick thread to capture the safety-net idea for continuous batching. we keep losing tails during noisy coalescing bursts. need a clear escape hatch and accounting model.

mika: agree, we've been reactive. propose a formal 'slowpath' with per-tenant tokens + enforced cap so it can't starve others.

jordan: draft behavior: admission tries to coalesce for up to T_coalesce ms. if no batch forms, admission returns SLOWPATH (with reason). runtime consults tenant ledger: if tokens>=cost, decrement and route to slowpath pipeline; else escalate to FASTPATH single-request funnel (pay more).

leah: note: slowpath pipeline still tries micro-batches but with tightened kv-warmup heuristics and prefix-bias. practically: prefer requests with prefix_length <= P_max to reduce kv misses.

mika: want to encode this hint in the request header: "prefix_hint": <int>. won't change public API, it's internal admission metadata.

arian: ledger model: token bucket per-tenant. params: capacity C, refill rate R, slowpath_cost S, fastpath_cost F (F > S). default: C=500, R=5/s, S=25, F=100 (tunable). these are starting points.

jordan: how do we prevent synchronized refills causing flash storms? we should jitter refill and add exponential backoff on repeated slowpath usage per tenant.

leah: observability: tag requests with path_taken:{COALESCE, SLOWPATH, FASTPATH} and include tenant_tier, headroom_remaining. add a histogram of headroom_balance.

mika: also emit an event when ledger dips below 10% so scheduler can preemptively shed work or request upstream rate-limit.

arian: handshake between batcher and scheduler: batcher can request a proactive drain by sending DRAIN_REQUEST(reason, severity). scheduler honors only after N consecutive requests or if global_headroom_low. prevents ping-pong.

jordan: algorithmic dampening: require k consecutive DRAIN_REQUESTs within window W to trigger. after trigger, impose min_drain_interval and decay timer. keeps oscillation down.

leah: streaming resume corner: if a streaming generation is interrupted and moved between pipelines, we must carry a compact resume token: {kv_cursor, prefix_len, partial_state_checksum}. minimal so it fits in tracing and doesn't leak model internals.

mika: ops playbook: if FASTPATH spikes, check slowpath_ratio per tenant. if a single tenant accounts for >X% escalations, temporarily reduce their refill R to R/2 and notify owner.

arian: testing matrix: synthetic workloads with Pareto tenant sizes, 5% tenants flagged as noisy. measure p50/p95/p99 latency, cost delta, and request distribution across pipelines. add chaos test that randomly disables coalescing for nodes.

jordan: i'll build a simple sim (python) using the bucket params and power-law arrivals. aim: p50 change <2%, p99 <10% and cost increase <8% for dedicated pools.

leah: rollout: feature-flag slowpath and ledger. default off for hosted, opt-in for dedicated. dashboards: slowpath_rate, escalation_rate, headroom_percentiles, draining_triggers.

mika: open design questions: 1) should slowpath be tenant-tier-aware at admission time or only ledger-weighted? 2) how to surface prefix_hint ergonomically from SDKs? 3) exact backoff curve for repeated slowpath usage.

arian: next steps: jordan -> sim results; leah -> telemetry changes; mika -> ops runbook draft; i'll write RFC follow-up with sequence diagrams and example metrics.

ci-bot: checklist: PRs required -> batcher:admission-exit-codes, scheduler:drain-api, runtime:slowpath-pipeline, infra:tenant-ledger, telemetry:slowpath-tags. reviewers -> @arian @mika @jordan @leah.

arian: thanks everyone. will squash into an RFC doc after sim numbers land.
